turns.en: But if you go back just a little further in time, rates were higher, realized returns were lower and some of the products that did exist back then in the mutual fund wrapper, they do have slightly higher fees, but still they've underperformed or they've just now broken even with just a regular US equity ETF going back to the 1990s.
turns.zh: 但只要你稍微往前看一点：那时候利率更高、实现回报更低。当年还存在的一些产品——以共同基金的形式包装——费率略高一点，但一直跑输，或者直到今天才刚刚追平一只普通的美股 ETF，从 1990 年代算起。

turns.en: There's a pretty severe recency bias where the products that people can easily see and access look really, really good, but it's because of a very specific set of factors over that period of time and it's not always going to work out that well.
turns.zh: 这里有非常严重的近因偏误（recency bias）：人们容易看到、容易买到的那批产品看起来特别棒，只是因为那段时间一系列特定因素恰好如此，它不会永远这么奏效。

turns.en: If you're going to do that, you don't want to have any cash sitting around. You don't want to have 30% of your account in cash and then have 70% in a leveraged ETF, which a lot of people can do that.
turns.zh: 如果你要做这个，就别让账上趴着现金。你不要账户里 30% 现金、70% 杠杆 ETF，很多人还真就这么干。

turns.en: I think leveraged ETF, futures, some of the low margin cost brokerages all can get you to probably 1% over risk-free rates, but even if expected returns of equities is 2% over risk-free rates, that doesn't mean you should do it because you have to think about what's the risk-adjusted return at the margin of owning the equities and in general, that's always going to be lower than the expected return.
turns.zh: 我觉得杠杆 ETF、期货、一些低保证金成本的券商，大概都能让你做到无风险利率之上 1% 左右。但就算股票预期回报比无风险利率高 2%，也不意味着你该加杠杆，因为你要想：在持有股票的边际上，风险调整后的回报是多少？而一般来说，边际风险调整后的回报总是低于预期回报。

turns.en: The risk-adjusted return is always lower. It can never go the other way because risk is always a cost. It just starts to get really marginal, I think, very quickly.
turns.zh: 风险调整后的回报总是更低的，它永远不会反过来，因为风险本身就是一种成本。我觉得这笔账很快就变得非常勉强了。

turns.en: In a different world, a different environment, if CAPE or 15 earnings yield was high and interest rates were low and risk premium was high, it could look a bit different, but there's plenty of risk.
turns.zh: 换一个世界、换一种环境：如果 CAPE 或者 15 倍盈利的收益率很高、利率很低、风险溢价很高，情况看起来就有点不一样，但那里依然有大量的风险。

turns.en: If you're close to 100% in equities, that's a lot of risk. That's another thing I would say is that's just a lot of risk. It doesn't feel like a lot of risk today, but one day you'll wake up and it's going to be a lot of risk and it's a lot of return.
turns.zh: 如果你接近 100% 都在股票里，那是非常大的风险。这也是我想强调的一点：这就是很大的风险。今天感觉不到风险有多大，但总有一天你一觉醒来，会发现那是非常大的风险、也是非常大的回报。

turns.en: If markets keep going up and you had 100% in equities, you'll do really well. The human capital argument for young people is also really interesting because it makes sense.
turns.zh: 如果市场继续涨而你 100% 持有股票，你会赚得很好。年轻人的人力资本论点对年轻人确实很有意思，因为它讲得通。

turns.en: The Mertenshire argument for leverage makes sense for a young person, but then you start thinking about what does the human capital of a young person actually look like?
turns.zh: Merton share 的论证对年轻人加杠杆是讲得通的。但接下来你得想：年轻人的实际人力资本到底长什么样？

turns.en: Is it really bond-like for someone entering the workforce? I don't know that it is. I don't think anything is totally bond-like. There's always going to be some beta in there.
turns.zh: 一个刚进职场的人，他的人力资本真的像债券吗？我不觉得。我也不觉得有任何东西真的完全像债券。里面总有 beta。

turns.en: A lot of times, the person that's thinking about leverage is the person who has high beta human capital, too. It's the person working in tech.
turns.zh: 很多时候，琢磨着要加杠杆的那个人，恰好也是人力资本 beta 很高的人。比如在科技公司上班的人。

turns.en: The person that's got a trading job in Wall Street or something. So many of the people are people with high beta human capital. You also have all the people that are just doing it for a living, influencers and so on that are out there.
turns.zh: 比如在华尔街做交易员的那种人。很多人的人力资本 beta 都很高。还有那些把它当饭吃的人——网红之类，也大有人在。

turns.en: It's not totally clear what their human capital is deriving from other than things that are pretty economy sensitive. There's the beta for sure, but then there's also the tails.
turns.zh: 他们的人力资本到底来自什么，并不清楚，但大体上肯定是对经济周期很敏感的东西。Beta 是确定的，但还有尾部。

turns.en: If you look at software developers right now, there's just a lot of folks who I think are realizing their human capital was a lot riskier than they maybe thought it was just because of what AI is doing to that profession.
turns.zh: 你要是看看现在的软件开发者，就会很多人意识到：他们的人力资本其实比他们原先以为的风险大得多，就因为 AI 正在对那个行业动手。

turns.en: So you've got a new book that you mentioned early on in this conversation, Get Rich Once and Other Financial Wisdom for Our Younger Selves. So to finish off our conversation here, what financial wisdom would you give to your younger self?
turns.zh: 你前面提过一本新书：Get Rich Once and Other Financial Wisdom for Our Younger Selves。那作为我们这次对话的收尾，你会给年轻时的自己什么理财智慧？

turns.en: Oh, I'm embarrassed to say this, but I would say, read a book like this. Do something proactive to make a plan and to really think about your finances.
turns.zh: 唉，说出来我自己都害臊：我会说，去读一本这样的书吧。主动做点什么，做一个计划，认真想想你的财务。

turns.en: And I say that it sounds so obvious in a way, but I can tell you that when I started in Wall Street in 1984, I went for a really long time without thinking about my personal financial situation.
turns.zh: 我知道这话说起来显而易见，但我要告诉你：我 1984 年进华尔街之后，过了非常久都没有认真考虑过自己的个人财务状况。

turns.en: I was busy. I was doing well. I was dating and I just didn't do it. And I had learned this stuff in university. I studied finance and university, but there was some kind of disconnect between leaving university working in Wall Street where I just didn't think about this stuff.
turns.zh: 我很忙，混得还不错，还在谈恋爱，反正就是没去想。我在大学学的是金融，这些我都学过，但从大学到华尔街工作之间好像断了一环，我就是不去想这些事。

turns.en: And so I would say, whether you read our book, there's so many ways today to make yourself really financially literate and to give yourself enough financial sophistication so that you can make a plan.
turns.zh: 所以我会说：不管读不读我们的书，今天有太多方法能让你真正具备金融素养、给自己足够的金融成熟度，好去做出一个规划。

turns.en: You can make a lifetime plan. You can get your financial affairs in order and you can do all of that in the time it takes to watch one season of your favorite Netflix series.
turns.zh: 你可以做一个终身计划，把你的财务事务理清楚。而这些事情花的时间，也就够你刷完一季你最喜欢的 Netflix 剧集。

turns.en: In 10 hours, you can just really have your whole situation sorted out. This is how much I really need to save. I'm doing the best with my 401k match or whatever we have in Canada.
turns.zh: 10 个小时，你就能把整个局面理得明明白白：我到底需要存多少，我 401(k) 的 match 拿满了没有，或者在加拿大对应的叫什么来着。

turns.en: All of these things, they are simple, but it just takes some time. We should all be doing that. And besides our book, there's so many other, our forthcoming book.
turns.zh: 所有这些事情都很简单，但你就是得花点时间。我们每个人都该去做。除了我们的书——我那本还没出版的书——

turns.en: There's so much other resources out there for people to use to get there. There's parents, there's other elders, there's other colleagues, there's other friends.
turns.zh: 外面还有太多其他资源可以用。有父母，有长辈，有同事，有朋友。

turns.en: It's just a question of being intentional and devoting that time to it because it's amazing how many of us didn't do it and how many people are not doing it today.
turns.zh: 关键是你得有意识地、把那点时间投进去。因为太多人没做过这件事——包括我自己——今天还有太多人没在做。

turns.en: You said you were embarrassed to reference your own book as the resource. I don't know, man. I was doing an interview for a newspaper recently and they asked me the same question and I thought about it and I was like, you know what?
turns.zh: 你说过你不好意思把自家书当资源推荐。是吗。我最近接受一家报纸的采访，他们问了同样的问题，我想了一下，然后说：你知道吗？

turns.en: They should listen to this podcast. Absolutely. If you're producing good information, you should tell people to consume it. It's not an embarrassing thing.
turns.zh: 他们该去听这档播客。当然。如果你在产出好的信息，你就该告诉大家去消费它。这不是什么丢人的事。

turns.en: So many of my friends are huge fans of your podcast. Absolutely. It's a great way for people to get educated and there's great stuff out there.
turns.zh: 我的很多朋友都是你们播客的超级粉丝。绝对的。这是人们接受教育的好方式，而且外面有很多好东西。

turns.en: It's just being intentional about going after it and doing the right thing. It matters. We hear, and it's not just our podcast, like you said, there's lots of good stuff out there, but we hear from people who they'll email Cameron and I and they'll say like, you changed my life.
turns.zh: 关键是有意地去追求它、做正确的事。这很重要。我们收到过反馈——不只是我们播客，像你所说，外面好东西很多——但经常有人给 Cameron 和我发邮件说：你们改变了我的人生。

turns.en: You completely changed the course of my life just by having good information and they're making financial decisions more confidently now. It's like, it matters, but the resources are out there.
turns.zh: 就因为提供了好的信息，你们彻底改变了我人生的走向。他们现在做财务决策更自信了。这说明信息真的有用，但资源本来就在外面。

turns.en: You just have to dedicate the time to consuming them. Super rewarding for all of us, for sure. 100%. Well, it's a good place to finish, Victor.
turns.zh: 你只是得花时间把它消费掉。对我们所有人来说，这都是超级有回报的。绝对的。好，Victor，这是个完美的收尾。

turns.en: We really appreciate you coming back on the podcast. This is a great conversation. Thank you both very much. Hope to see you guys in person before long too.
turns.zh: 我们非常感谢你再回到播客。这是很棒的一次对谈。太感谢你们俩了。希望不久之后能跟你们线下见面。

turns.en: Definitely. That'd be nice. Thanks, Victor. Thanks, guys. That was something. Yeah. Trying to think like, how do you encapsulate that conversation?
turns.zh: 当然，那一定很好。谢谢你，Victor。谢了各位。这期真够劲的。是啊，我在想该怎么总结这期对话？

turns.en: I wrote down the line and he basically off Mike said the exact same thing, which is there's so much to talk about in a market portfolio environment.

turns.en: Yeah. And it's true. Yeah. It is true. We covered so much ground. I love talking about super nerdy stuff. You were messaging me as we were going about how their nerds are getting their fill and they were, but the whole conversation about direct indexing, super interesting.
turns.zh: 是啊，确实如此，真的如此。我们聊了那么多。我特别喜欢聊这些极客话题。你录制途中一直在给我发信息，说极客听众这回听得过瘾，还真是。但整个关于直接指数化的对话，太有意思了。

turns.en: His paper on who killed the random walk. Also fascinating just thinking about where the different market anomalies come from and where the different return premiums come from that we see in the market and kind of thinking about who is responsible for that.
turns.zh: 他那篇 Who Killed the Random Walk 的论文也特别引人入胜。想想不同的市场异象从何而来、我们看到的种种回报溢价从何而来，想想谁该为此负责——

turns.en: What's going on at the investor level is causing the anomalies that we see. Their little study they did on whether you can predict returns from tomorrow's news.
turns.zh: 是投资者层面正在发生什么，制造了我们看到的这些异象。还有他们做的那个小研究：能不能用明天的新闻预测回报。

turns.en: Super interesting. Like that's such a cool experiment to run. I mean, tomorrow's news today, I had no idea they'd been done that many times, but that's pretty amazing.
turns.zh: 超级有意思，这么实验太酷了。我是说拿今天的消息去预测明天，我都不知道这已经被做了这么多次了，真厉害。

turns.en: And even AI couldn't really take advantage of it. I love the discussion on leverage. That's something I've been looking at quite a bit recently and I think Victor's thoughts are so good.
turns.zh: 连 AI 都占不到什么便宜。我很喜欢关于杠杆的讨论。这也是我最近一直在研究的话题，我觉得 Victor 的想法真好。

turns.en: He applies that just the Merton share thinking so well to so many of these topics. I'm glad that we talk a little bit about what the Merton share is and what it means and why investors should care about it during the conversation.
turns.zh: 他把 Merton share 的思维用得那么好，套进这么多话题里。很高兴我们在对话里讲了讲 Merton share 是什么、意味着什么、为什么投资者该关心它。

turns.en: So Victor, we mentioned the introduction. He is the founder of Elm Wealth. They've also got an ETF out through their firm that's doing position sizing based on Merton share thinking.
turns.zh: Victor 这人，我们在开头介绍过。他是 Elm Wealth 的创始人。他们公司还发行了一只 ETF，基于 Merton share 的思路做仓位规模。

turns.en: So they're using expected returns and volatilities over time to change the allocation between equities and fixed income, which is kind of neat, but they've also got a wealth practice as I understand it.
turns.zh: 他们随时间用预期回报和波动率来调整股票和固收之间的配置，这挺妙的。而且据我了解，他们也有一条财富管理的业务线。

turns.en: And Victor was one of the founding partners of long-term capital management, which is a very academic hedge fund. A bunch of academics were involved that collapsed in 1998 quite spectacularly.
turns.zh: Victor 还是 Long-Term Capital Management 的创始合伙人之一，那是一支非常学院派的对冲基金。一堆学术明星参与其中，1998 年崩盘，崩得相当惨烈。

turns.en: To say the least. To say the least. We talked in our last episode, episode 270 with Victor about kind of that experience and how it shaped his thinking and the rest of his career after that event.
turns.zh: 至少可以这么说。至少可以这么说。我们上次和 Victor 的那期——第 270 期——聊过那段经历如何塑造了他之后的思考和整个职业生涯。

turns.en: But I remember the first time Victor reached out to us, I knew him as a character in that story about long-term capital management. He was in the book.
turns.zh: 但我记得 Victor 第一次联系我们时，我对他的认知就是 Long-Term Capital Management 那个故事里的一个人物。他就是那本书里的角色。

turns.en: Yeah. So I was blown away when he reached out, but he's very thoughtful. It's neat to see him doing research that's getting into some journals.
turns.zh: 是啊，所以他联系我的时候我惊呆了。不过他真的非常善于思考。看到他做的研究能上期刊，真好。

turns.en: Great thoughts from him on all those topics. Good guy and a great communicator, so it's really nice to have him on. Yep. Anything else? No, I think that's good.
turns.zh: 他在所有这些话题上的想法都很出色。好人，又是出色的沟通者，请他来真好。还有别的吗？没有了，我觉得差不多了。
